title: add-skim-logs-and-cost-density-explorer
author: Aisha Kumar
release_notes: Added sampled invocation frames ("skim logs") to reduce log volume while preserving investigatory context; new 'Cost Density Explorer' Grafana dashboard for spotting concentrated token-cost spikes; new alert 'cost-density-spike' with tuned hysteresis; no breaking API changes.
description:
Motivation: Our current full-invocation logging produces large volumes and makes it hard to locate cost-concentrated anomalies in the long tail. This PR introduces two complementary observability features: (1) a compact sampled logging format ("skim logs" / invocation frames) that captures a lightweight summary of each invocation with token-anchor pointers, and (2) a Cost Density Explorer dashboard that visualizes per-invocation token-cost concentration as a delta matrix + sparkline, enabling SREs and engineers to spot requests where a small subset of tokens account for disproportionate cost.

What changed (high level):
- Implemented a new log serializer (invocation_skim_frame) that emits compact frames for a configurable sample fraction; frames include: invocation_id, model_variant, total_tokens, top_token_spans (start,end,label,count,cost_estimate), cpu/gpu_time_ms, kv_cache_hit_ratio, and an obfuscated prompt hash for correlation.
- Added reservoir-based sampler in runtime (continuous-bounded reservoir) to maintain representative sketch of long-tail invocations across tenants. Sampler is weight-aware (weights by token-cost) to bias retention toward cost-heavy invocations without siloing to single tenants.
- Promoted a new metric: redwood_invocation_cost_density_bucketed (histogram) and redwood_invocation_token_concentration (gauge with tags) to represent fraction of cost in top 1/5/10 token spans.
- Created Grafana dashboard 'Cost Density Explorer' with: matrix panel (invocation x token-bin delta), heatmap of token-concentration percentiles, per-tenant sparklines, and drilldowns to sampled skim logs and traces.
- New alert: observability:cost-density-spike - triggers when p99 of token-concentration > threshold for N minutes and absolute cost > tenant baseline; includes automatic annotation linking sample frames and related traces.
- Backwards compatibility: default sampler rate keeps current log volume stable; skim frames are opt-in per-tenant via console (flag: observability.skim_logs.enabled) but sampling and metrics are enabled cluster-wide to allow cross-tenant rollups.

Why this is different: Instead of logging full token sequences or heavy KV dumps, skim logs provide a compact investigatory breadcrumb that preserves where cost is concentrated (token spans) and ties to trace IDs and prompt hashes. Combined with density metrics, this makes it fast to locate root causes (e.g., prompts that trigger degenerate loop generation or quantization fallback churn) without increasing log retention costs.

Checklist (what I did):
- [x] Runtime sampler implementation + unit tests for reservoir invariants
- [x] Compact JSON schema for invocation_skim_frame and serializer with size limit enforcement
- [x] Metrics instrumentation (histogram + gauge) and prometheus exporter wiring
- [x] Grafana dashboard JSON + panels with drilldown links to log/trace UIs
- [x] Alert definition with sane defaults and runbook link
- [x] Migration notes and console toggle for per-tenant opting
- [x] Load-tested on staging with aggregated 24h replay (no >2% increase in logging ingress)

Testing and observations:
- Staging replay (50k invocations): sampler retained ~1.2k skim frames; retention biased toward top-cost invocations as intended.
- End-to-end tracing links worked for ~99.6% of frames (missing cases due to ~0.4% trace propagation failures already known under ENG-912).
- Dashboard panels render at scale; initial alerts fired in staging for simulated degenerate prompts and latched correctly with hysteresis.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main gated by CI (done).
2) Enable cluster-wide metrics and dashboard for internal tenants (0 -> 100% metrics).
3) Enable skim-logs sampler default rate 0.1% across tenants for 48h to validate cardinality and cost.
4) Flip per-tenant opt-in in console for customers who want frames forwarded to their log retention bucket.
5) Revisit thresholds after 2 weeks of production telemetry, adjust alert:cost-density-spike thresholds per-tenant baseline.

Operational notes:
- Sampler config exposed via runtime configmap and console feature flag; pay attention to "sampler.weight_cutoff" when tenant cost distributions are skewed.
- Skim frames contain an obfuscated prompt hash; do not log raw prompt content unless tenant has opted into storing prompt text. This preserves privacy defaults.
- If tenants forward frames to external sinks, they will see compact token-span descriptors only.

Related: ENG-925 (observability long-tail work), SUP-451 (customer-reported high log costs), ENG-931 (tracing propagation fixes).
